correctness.rationale: The published CDF is F(x)=log(1+g)e^{beta(g-1)}/log2 with g=e^{-(alpha/x)^theta}. Its printed Eq(13) surrogate chooses z_q=W_0(beta q e^beta log2)/beta (equivalently unique z in (0,1) with z e^{beta(z-1)}=q log2), hence F(Qtilde(q))=q log(1+z_q)/z_q<q. As q approaches 1, z_q approaches z_beta<1 satisfying z_beta e^{beta(z_beta-1)}=log2; thus Qtilde is bounded while exact quantile diverges. Because z_beta is in (log2,1), limiting achieved coverage c_beta=log(1+z_beta)/z_beta belongs to (log2, log(1+log2)/log2). Expanding exact CDF at g=1 gives 1-F(x)~(beta+1/(2log2))(alpha/x)^theta; hence Q_exact(q)~alpha[(beta+1/(2log2))/(1-q)]^{1/theta}. Independent monotone bisection for alpha=theta=beta=1, q=.99 gave surrogate 5.0654970551, exact 171.0287464965 and coverage .7227998524. This is source equation evaluation, not claim about unknown software or empirical VaR figures.

Demonstrating that a proposed high-confidence VaR cutoff remains bounded while the correct quantile diverges, with exact coverage ceiling and asymptotic correction, has direct implications for tail-risk calibration; more than a cheap algebraic typo check.
